name: Two Knights Defense (as Black)
desc: Meet the Italian with the active 3...Nf6. Learn to survive 4.Ng5 with the main line 5...Na5, handle the quiet 4.d3, the sharp 4.d4 lines and the fork trick against 4.Nc3.

lines.name: 4.Ng5 main line 5...Na5
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 {The Two Knights: counter-attacking e4.} 4.Ng5 d5 {The only good defense.} 5.exd5 Na5 {Never 5...Nxd5? 6.Nxf7! — the Fried Liver.} 6.Bb5+ c6 7.dxc6 bxc6 8.Be2 h6 {Kicking the knight.} 9.Nf3 e4 10.Ne5 Bd6 {Excellent compensation for the pawn: space and development.}

lines.name: 4.Ng5 6.d3 (Kieseritzky)
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Ng5 d5 5.exd5 Na5 6.d3 h6 7.Nf3 e4 8.Qe2 Nxc4 {Grabbing the bishop pair.} 9.dxc4 Bc5 {Rapid development compensates for the pawn.}

lines.name: Quiet 4.d3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d3 Be7 {A solid setup.} 5.O-O O-O 6.Re1 d6 7.c3 Na5 {Hunting the Italian bishop.} 8.Bb5 a6 9.Ba4 b5 10.Bc2 c5 {Gaining queenside space.}

lines.name: 4.d4 exd4 5.O-O (Modern)
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.O-O Nxe4 {Taking the pawn.} 6.Re1 d5 7.Bxd5 Qxd5 8.Nc3 Qa5 {The queen escapes the pin.} 9.Nxe4 Be6 10.Neg5 O-O-O {Black castles into safety with a good game.}

lines.name: 4.d4 exd4 5.e5
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5.e5 d5 {Counter-attacking the bishop.} 6.Bb5 Ne4 7.Nxd4 Bd7 8.Bxc6 bxc6 9.O-O Be7 {Black has a healthy position.}

lines.name: 4.Nc3 fork trick
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.Nc3 Nxe4! {The fork trick.} 5.Nxe4 d5 {Forking bishop and knight.} 6.Bd3 dxe4 7.Bxe4 Bd6 {Black has a free and easy game.}

name: Petrov's Defense (as Black)
desc: The Russian Defense: Black counter-attacks e4 instead of defending e5. Super-solid and loved by elite players. Learn the key move order 3...d6 and how to punish the Cochrane Gambit.

lines.name: Classical 5.d4 main line
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 {First kick the knight! 3...Nxe4? 4.Qe2! is a known trap.} 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.d4 d5 6.Bd3 Nc6 7.O-O Be7 8.c4 Nb4 {Hitting the d3 bishop.} 9.Be2 O-O 10.Nc3 Bf5 {Solid and active.}

lines.name: 5.Nc3 symmetrical
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 5.Nc3 Nxc3 6.dxc3 Be7 7.Be3 Nc6 8.Qd2 Be6 9.O-O-O Qd7 {Mirror castling plans; equal but sharp.}

lines.name: Cochrane Gambit 4.Nxf7?!
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 d6 4.Nxf7?! {The Cochrane Gambit: a dubious piece sacrifice.} Kxf7 5.Nc3 c5! {Controlling d4.} 6.Bc4+ Be6 7.Bxe6+ Kxe6 8.d4 Kf7 {The king walks back to safety; Black's extra piece should tell.}

lines.name: Steinitz 3.d4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.d4 Nxe4 4.Bd3 d5 5.Nxe5 Nd7 {Challenging the strong knight.} 6.Nxd7 Bxd7 7.O-O Bd6 8.c4 c6 {Solid and equal.}

lines.name: Four Knights 3.Nc3
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nc3 Nc6 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Bb4 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Bd3 d5 8.exd5 cxd5 9.O-O O-O {Active pieces for Black.}

lines.name: Boden-Kieseritzky 3.Bc4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Bc4 Nxe4 4.Nc3 Nxc3 5.dxc3 f6 {Holding e5 solidly; don't let White's lead in development scare you.}

name: Stafford Gambit (as Black)
desc: A tricky gambit from the Petrov: Black sacrifices the e-pawn for quick development and a minefield of traps. Objectively dubious, but deadly in blitz. Learn every trap and the natural mistakes White makes.

lines.name: Trap: 6.Bg5?? Nxe4! mate
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6!? {The Stafford Gambit.} 4.Nxc6 dxc6 {Recapture towards the center, opening the bishop and queen.} 5.d3 Bc5 {Aiming at f2.} 6.Bg5?? {Pinning the knight... or so White thinks.} Nxe4! {The queen sacrifice!} 7.Bxd8 Bxf2+ 8.Ke2 Bg4# {Checkmate!}

lines.name: Trap: 6.Bg5 Nxe4 7.dxe4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3 Bc5 6.Bg5?? Nxe4! 7.dxe4 Bxf2+! {Deflecting the king from the d-file.} 8.Kxf2 Qxd1 {Black wins the queen.}

lines.name: Trap: 5.e5 Ne4 6.d4 Qh4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.e5 Ne4 {The knight is strong on e4.} 6.d4 Qh4 {Threatening ...Qxf2#.} 7.g3? Nxg3! 8.fxg3 Qe4+ {A fork on the long diagonal.} 9.Qe2 Qxh1 {Black wins the rook.}

lines.name: Trap: 6.Be2 h5 7.O-O? Ng4
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nxc6 dxc6 5.d3 Bc5 6.Be2 h5 {Preparing ...Ng4 and opening the h-file.} 7.O-O? Ng4 8.h3? Qd6! {Threatening ...Qh2#.} 9.hxg4 hxg4 {The h-file opens: ...Qh2# is coming and White is lost.}

lines.name: 4.Nf3: regaining the pawn
lines.moves: 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nf6 3.Nxe5 Nc6 4.Nf3 Nxe4 {Black simply regains the pawn with a free game.}
